ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all proposed directors, officers, registered shareholder UBOs and authorised representatives against the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, OFAC Non-SDN Sectoral Sanctions, HM Treasury consolidated sanctions, the EU consolidated list, and internationally recognised PEP databases. Screening is calibrated to FINTRAC obligations under the PCMLTFA regarding politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign) and to enhanced due diligence requirements for higher-risk jurisdictions or complex ownership structures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services – Corporate Online
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English or a transliteration into Latin alphabetic characters; the official name must contain one of the mandatory unlimited liability suffixes, e.g. 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', 'Unlimited', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée' or 'SRI'. A name cannot be confusing with an existing name, cannot be identical except for punctuation, and must avoid any term or expression that is prohibited or requires ministerial consent unless such consent has been obtained. A NUANS search must be conducted and the resulting report attached to the name request.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the BC Registrar, the incorporator may either file a revised name request with corrected information or appeal the decision by submitting a written request for reconsideration to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the rejection notice, including a statement of the grounds for why the name should be approved and any additional supporting evidence. A name reservation may be extended before its expiry by filing a further name request and paying the renewal fee; absent such extension, the reservation lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the registered office only if it is a physical street address in British Columbia, accessible for service of process during normal business hours, and properly maintained by a registered agent or corporate service provider. For a ULC engaged in CO2 laser-cutting and assembly, the production facility cannot be virtual; municipal zoning, occupational health and safety, and product-safety compliance must be satisfied at the actual business premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: estimated 8% annual probability of an unannounced inspection of the registered office address, and approximately 25% annual probability of an unannounced municipal or WorkSafeBC occupational-health and fire-safety inspection of the assembly facility due to presence of industrial laser equipment.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57; Incorporation and articles ss. 10–15; Notice of Articles s. 51; Registered office and records s. 198; Directors and officers ss. 29–38; Unlimited liability company provisions applicable to ULC entity class.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, operating through BC Registries and Online Services.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Incorporation Application and Form 2 – Notice of Articles, submitted together with the filed Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under British Columbia law; shares may be issued without par value for any consideration fixed by directors, and no escrow account or capital contribution block is required for an ordinary ULC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby adopt the Company’s Articles and approve the issuance of common shares to each subscriber at the consideration set in the share subscription agreements. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office and records office of the Company be fixed at the physical address in British Columbia designated in the Notice of Articles. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors named in the Notice of Articles be and are hereby elected as the initial directors. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed President, and [Name] be appointed Corporate Secretary and Treasurer. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors be and are hereby authorized to open and operate bank accounts, execute banking resolutions, and complete all governmental registrations necessary to begin operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services – Name Request Online (bcregistry.ca/name-request)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search against British Columbia and federal databases; submit a Name Request with the legal element 'ULC'. If approved, BC Registry issues a name reservation valid for 56 days. Proceed with incorporation before the reservation expires.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Request form or electronic submission
Corporate name search or NUANS report
Mailing and physical address for the proposed corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, select a changed distinctive element or obtain written consent from the existing name holder; re-file within the reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal preparer and BC Registry e-filing system (Corporate Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles for an Unlimited Liability Corporation, including share structure and transfer restrictions; complete Notice of Articles (Form 2) naming the registered office, records office, and initial directors; obtain signed consents from directors and officers.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director form
Consent to act as officer form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory review identifies missing or invalid clauses, amend the draft Articles and Notice of Articles and resubmit before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry – Corporate Online (bcregistry.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 1 – Incorporation Application together with the Notice of Articles through Corporate Online using the reserved name. Pay the prescribed filing fee by approved electronic method and request issuance of the electronic Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for incompleteness, respond to the Registry error report, correct the stated deficiencies, and refile; priority may be preserved if corrected within fifteen days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry – BC Registries Online Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation through the Corporate Online portal; record the company number and incorporation date; verify that the registered office and records office addresses shown are correct; download the official certified certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed or contains typographical errors, apply to the Corporate Registry for correction of records under section 24 of the Business Corporations Act, providing a supporting affidavit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Resolution and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial directors and incorporators of the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or execute a written resolution; adopt the first board resolution; issue share certificates; appoint officers; open the central securities register and records office; execute share subscription agreements and collect stated consideration.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written consent
Minute book and central securities register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer declines appointment, execute a supplemental unanimous board resolution and file a Notice of Director Change (Form 3) with the Corporate Registry within the statutory timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, WorkSafeBC, and Municipal Administrative Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; BC Ministry of Finance; WorkSafeBC; municipal business licence office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles, obtain a CRA Business Number for GST/HST, payroll, and corporate income tax; register the BC provincial corporate account; register as an employer with WorkSafeBC; apply for and obtain the municipal business licence and occupancy approval for the laser assembly premises.
required_dossiers: Business premises lease or ownership evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency notice is issued by CRA, WorkSafeBC, or the municipality, submit the required corrective schedule or pay the assessed administrative fee, then obtain written confirmation of compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Business Licence Office for the applicable British Columbia municipality; WorkSafeBC for occupational health and safety; BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy for environmental compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Industrial Business Licence for Light Manufacturing – Wooden Puzzle Laser Assembly

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Environmental Protection Division, Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full environmental assessment review; subject to site-specific waste discharge registration and municipal sewer/air emission permits if process discharges exceed regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Air emissions: local exhaust ventilation and filtration must achieve at least 95% capture efficiency for laser-generated particulate and volatile organic compounds; ambient PM2.5 must not exceed BC 24-hour objective of 25 µg/m³; VOC abatement required where annual emissions exceed 2 tonnes. Wastewater: any equipment-cleaning water must comply with municipal sewer bylaw pH 6.0–9.0, total suspended solids ≤ 350 mg/L, and oil and grease ≤ 50 mg/L; no unprented direct discharge to waterways. Solid waste: scrap wood must be recycled or lawfully landfilled; laser filter media containing hazardous residues must be classified and disposed as special waste under applicable BC regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and fire marshal inspection under the BC Fire Code; building occupancy permit verifying structural load capacity for laser cutting equipment; electrical safety inspection for all installed equipment; WorkSafeBC occupational clearance covering laser beam hazard controls, local exhaust ventilation, noise exposure, emergency stop systems, and staff training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) – My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of the BC unlimited liability corporation (ULC), the entity must apply to the CRA through the Business Registration Online (BRO) service to obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and applicable program accounts (e.g., GST/HST, payroll, import/export). The application requires the certificate of incorporation, registered office address, director/officer information, and the ULC's organizational documents. Non-resident owners must designate a Canadian resident representative for the receipt of CRA notices and service of process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A foreign-owned ULC may elect under subsection 216.1(1) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) to be treated as a corporation for all purposes of the Act, thereby preventing the application of domestic hybrid mismatch treatment that would otherwise cause the ULC to be disregarded as a separate taxpayer. Alternatively, in the absence of a timely s.216.1 election, the ULC may be treated as a flow-through entity for Canadian tax purposes to the extent of its foreign owners. Additional hybrid mismatch elections under Part XII.6 of the Income Tax Act may be relevant for cross-border arrangements involving the BC ULC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); in British Columbia, federal GST applies at 5% and provincial Retail Sales Tax (PST) is administered separately at 7%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (worldwide annual taxable supplies from all taxable supplies; the 'small supplier' threshold triggering mandatory GST/HST registration for non-resident and resident entities alike)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time electronic invoice clearance, pre-clearance API filing, or digital stamping for GST/HST. Invoices must include prescribed information (per section 169 of the Excise Tax Act) and electronic records must be retained in a readable and retrievable format for CRA audit. Voluntary e-invoicing via PEPPOL or similar networks is permitted, but no fiscal clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible personal property (including wooden puzzles) to non-resident customers are zero-rated for GST/HST under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act (section 1, Part V). Services supplied to a non-resident may also be zero-rated where the services are performed for a recipient who is a non-resident and the supply is not subject to ordinary Canadian consumption rules. For zero-rating, the supplier must satisfy the two-part test: (i) the property is exported pursuant to a supply made to a non-resident; and (ii) adequate evidence of export is obtained (e.g., commercial invoice, bill of lading, customs declaration, or third-party transportation records). Online sales fulfilled from Canadian inventory to foreign buyers via platforms such as Amazon or Stripe must be supported by export documentation and treated as zero-rated, subject to CRA's administrative guidelines.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A/Canadian Export Declaration)
Inward Remittance Certificate (or equivalent proof of foreign payment)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may audit export zero-rating claims and require production of all transport, customs, and payment documentation. Failure to substantiate exports results in reversal of the zero-rating, net tax reassessment, arrears interest, and penalties under sections 280 and 285 of the Excise Tax Act, including a penalty of 25% of the net tax amount for knowingly making false statements, plus gross negligence penalties of up to 50% of the understated net tax. Fraudulent zero-rating schemes may expose directors and owners to additional civil liability and criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act and Criminal Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Canada has operated a freely floating exchange-rate regime since 1951 and accepted IMF Article VIII obligations; there is no designated foreign-exchange control authority issuing convertibility licences or capital-transaction approvals. Prudential supervision of chartered banks is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act, while the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) supervises anti-money-laundering (AML) and terrorist-financing compliance under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). The Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), supervised by the Bank of Canada, now regulates retail payment service providers, complementing the Lynx/ACSS settlement architecture operated by Payments Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility for both capital and current account transactions. No pre-approval is required for direct foreign investment into a British Columbia Unlimited Liability Corporation (CA_ULC); a post-closing Investment Canada Act notification applies to WTO investors acquiring control of a Canadian business above the enterprise-value threshold (approximately CAD 5,000,000 for 2025), and the ULC is below that threshold in this atomic task. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, interest, royalty and management-fee payments to non-residents are unrestricted from an exchange-control perspective, but remain subject to Part XIII Income Tax Act non-resident withholding tax (statutory 25%, potentially treaty-reduced) and, in the case of a ULC, to Canada's pass-through eligibility and the entity-classification uncertainties faced by unlimited liability corporations in cross-border tax treaty application.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender, no statutory repatriation timeline, no conversion ratio, and no requirement to route export receipts through a domestic bank. A BC ULC manufacturing wooden 3D puzzles (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930) may freely invoice in CAD, USD or any other freely convertible currency, retain export proceeds in foreign-currency bank accounts, and use those proceeds directly for offshore supplier payments or physical USD clearing. The only binding obligations are FINTRAC record-keeping and reporting thresholds (including electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more), IFRS accounting recognition on the corporate balance sheet, and Canadian tax attribution in the hands of the shareholder for ULC pass-through purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.required_regulatory_filings_for_fx_trans: No exchange-control filings are required. FINTRAC EFT reports, T1135 foreign-income verification forms if applicable to the shareholder, Part XIII remittance returns (NR4), and BC Corporate Registry annual reports constitute the practical documentary compliance set.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Coast Capital Savings Federal Credit Union

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability rating: Medium-High for payment-orchestration and merchant treasury purposes only, not as the sole legal-entity banking relationship. A foreign or offshore electronic-money institution (EMI) is not a recognized deposit-taking institution under the Canadian Bank Act; it may not carry on the business of accepting deposits or describing itself as a bank in Canada. To serve a British Columbia ULC, an offshore EMI must either operate as a FINTRAC-registered money services business (MSB) or, for retail payment services provided to Canadian residents, register with the Bank of Canada as a payment service provider under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA). Wise Canada, Stripe Treasury and similar partners may provide segregated e-money balances and merchant settlement, but final CAD liquidity and legal-entity clearing must terminate in a Canadian chartered bank account or a Payments Canada clearing participant. Digital-only onboarding is viable through major banks, but the ULC should maintain a physical-nexus correspondent relationship for high-value SWIFT flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening with FINTRAC-compliant video interview, biometric identity verification and e-signature is generally available at the top-five Schedule I banks for directors resident in low-risk jurisdictions, including the United States and the United Kingdom. However, for a BC ULC with non-resident directors or shareholders, most banks will require at least one in-person or consular-notarized signatory verification, plus a live compliance interview with the AML officer. BC credit unions commonly mandate a physical branch interview. The bank may also require the ULC's sole or joint directors to appear at a Canadian embassy or consulate for identity verification if biometric credentials cannot be captured remotely. Practical mandate: plan for one physical appearance at a Vancouver branch or a notarized certificate executed before a recognized Canadian financial-services notary within the jurisdiction of the director's residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) opacity in the ULC shareholding chain, including offshore holding companies or discretionary trusts above the BC entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the BC Notice of Articles, corporate register of directors, the mandatory transparency register (if shareholder is a control person), notarized UBO attestation listing each natural person with 25%+ ownership or control, constitutional trust deeds and identity documents for trustees and beneficiaries, and the signed Canada Beneficial Ownership Transparency attestation form prepared by the incorporating counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director tax-residency mismatch or inconsistent CRS/FATCA self-certification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport with biographical page, national identity card, current CRS self-certification form (including any Canadian T1135/T1134 exposure statement), United States Form W-8BEN-E or UK Form W-8BEN-E where applicable, tax-residence certificate from the home tax authority, and a BC Corporate Registry extract confirming the director's lawful capacity to act for the ULC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for the initial cross-border equity injection, particularly where capital originates from personal savings, family loans or cryptocurrency liquidity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements from the remitting shareholder's regulated financial institution, a notarized share-subscription agreement or shareholder loan agreement, audited or reviewed financial statements of the ULC, and a complete wire-trail explanation from origin to RBC/TD account. Any cash component above CAD 10,000 must be avoided to prevent structuring red flags under PCMLTFA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control or product-safety screening triggered by the toy-manufacturing classification, laser equipment usage, or shipment to embargoed markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Harmonized System classification certificate confirming HS 9503.00 (wooden puzzles and toys), CCPSA (SOR/2018-82) compliance test report for children's products, supplier declarations confirming no restricted laser components or cryptographic software, an automated end-user/end-use due diligence screen against the Canadian Special Economic Measures Act list, OFAC SDN list and EU consolidated sanctions list, and monthly negative news screening maintained in the compliance file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The 'unlimited liability' label on the BC ULC triggers the bank's non-standard entity-risk model and may be misclassified as a high-risk pass-through vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal legal opinion from Canadian corporate counsel explaining BC ULC unlimited shareholder liability, purpose as a cross-border tax-pass-through vehicle, the absence of creditor-risk in the low-capital wooden-toy assembly business, and the ULC's annual BC Registry filings; if required, a parent-company guarantee or a subordination agreement to demonstrate credit support to the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be routed as SWIFT MT103 wire transfers in CAD or USD from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the RBC Capital Escrow Account or TD Operational Account using the exact legal beneficiary name CA__CA_BC__CA_ULC__ISIC_3240_07_WOODEN_PUZZLE_LASER_ASSEMBLY. The stated payment purpose should read 'Direct foreign investment - equity contribution to share capital of British Columbia ULC'. Canada imposes no government authorization or purpose-code approval for such wires; however, the remitting bank must be able to identify the transaction under FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000 or more), and the ULC should retain a board resolution, share-subscription agreement, and SWIFT transaction reference as the evidentiary chain. Large-value CAD clears through Payments Canada Lynx (real-time gross settlement), while USD inbound wires clear through Fedwire/CHIPS via the Canadian bank's US correspondent.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments to overseas suppliers of laser-cut wood components, packaging and hardware should use SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for commercial settlement or, for larger or documentary trades, Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) issued under UCP 600 with SWIFT MT700 messages. CAD-based domestic disbursements settle through Lynx for high value or ACSS for lower-value transactions. USD vendor payments clear through the Canadian bank's US clearing network (CHIPS or Fedwire). Amazon_Pay and Stripe merchant proceeds are aggregated by the payment processors and settled via sponsor-bank rails into the ULC's Canadian operating account; for Stripe Treasury, settlement ultimately rests on a Canadian Banking-as-a-Service sponsor bank arrangement. All outbound trade payments must be supported by commercial invoices, bill-of-lading or airway-bill evidence, and customs entry IDs where applicable, both to discharge FINTRAC monitoring and to support input-tax credits and Part XIII transaction characterization.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD foreign-exchange forward contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank, typically available for terms of one to twelve months without the need for collateral where the underlying is a known USD receivable or payable.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CAD/USD, technically permissible through OSFI-regulated dealers where physical settlement is operationally impractical or where the hedge references a restricted-currency basket; however, for fully convertible CAD these are generally unnecessary and bank quoting is limited.
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD basis swaps) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement for longer-dated pipeline hedging, debt-service alignment or shareholder-loan interest-rate management.

FX options, zero-cost collars and participating forwards to protect USD-denominated Amazon_Pay/Stripe settlement revenues while retaining upside participation, offered as OTC bilateral derivative transactions subject to bank credit approval and non-cleared margining rules where applicable.

Natural hedging through a USD-denominated operating account at Scotiabank or RBC, allowing the ULC to retain export proceeds in USD and disburse USD supplier payments directly, thereby reducing the derivative requirement without violating any Canadian FX-control rule.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, s. 274)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies - BC Registry Services (CORES online)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary of incorporation or of the last Annual Report filing; the due date resets each year to the last filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inability to obtain Certificate of Compliance; after 2 consecutive years in default the Registrar may strike off and dissolve the company (ss. 271-272); restoration (s. 277) requires court order and arrears payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and BC provincial corporate tax administered by CRA under tax collection agreement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after fiscal year-end; June 30 for a December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (max 12 months); minimum CA$100 if no tax payable; daily compound interest on balance; CRA can issue arbitrary assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (Excise Tax Act, RSC 1985, c. E-15) - available only if annual taxable supplies of the registrant and associated persons are CA$500,000 or less
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end for annual filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ETA s. 280 penalty: CA$250 per unfiled return plus CA$250 per day of continued non-filing (max 20 days); daily compound interest on net tax owing; CRA may assess on estimated amounts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: BC BCA s. 228 requires appointment of an auditor at each AGM for every BC company; no revenue-based threshold applies, but the obligation is dispensed if the shareholders pass a resolution waiving the auditor (unanimous resolution in practice); if not waived, a licensed public accountant audit is mandatory regardless of size
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) or ASPE (Part II) at the ULC's election; basis must be disclosed consistently and support the T2 and BC corporate tax computations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC BCA Part 5.1 (ss. 51.2-51.9) Transparency Register: identify every individual with significant control (>=25% of voting rights or market value, or de facto control); verify identity at entry; update within 15 days of any share-transfer or control change; annually reconcile the register at fiscal year-end and before filing the BC Annual Report; register is not filed publicly but must be provided to BC Registrar, CRA and law enforcement on demand; breach is an offence with fines up to CA$25,000 (individuals) and CA$50,000 (corporations)
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholder and director meetings and resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 150-500 (approx. USD 110-365) per year for a BC registered office and corporate agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 4,000-12,000 (approx. USD 2,900-8,800) for a small private ULC when an auditor is engaged; nil if audit is waived by unanimous shareholder resolution

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.0% combined (15% federal general + 12% British Columbia general); ULC is a Non-CCPC and does not qualify for the small business deduction
